headline: Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator CVE-2026-16812: CVSS 10.0 Command Injection Under Active Attack
summary: A critical CVSS 10.0 command injection vulnerability in on-premises Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) is under active exploitation. This flaw allows attackers to gain full control over SD-WAN deployments.
details: Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-16812, a CVSS 10.0 operating system command injection flaw in on-premises Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO). Arista confirmed external discovery and active exploitation when its advisory was published on July 27, 2026.

VCO serves as the management plane for VeloCloud SD-WAN deployments, controlling routing policy and holding device credentials. A compromised orchestrator can grant attackers access to all managed VeloCloud Edge devices.

The vulnerability stems from privileged internal functionality being remotely accessible without authentication, allowing attacker-supplied input into an OS command context. This classic pattern contributes to its maximum CVSS score.

The CVSS 10.0 rating signifies a network attack vector, low complexity, no privileges required, and no user interaction. It results in full impact to confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the orchestrator and its managed data.
Four VCO release branches are affected, specifically customer-operated on-premises deployments. Arista's hosted and dedicated VCO offerings were remediated in advance.

Operators must immediately block the identified attacker IPs (8.19.75.217, 206.72.242.124, 206.72.242.162) and check historical VCO web access logs for hits. A match indicates an incident, not just a scan.

Arista advises preserving all evidence, including web access, application, system, and database logs, before patching or rebuilding. Patching first can destroy crucial artifacts needed for forensic analysis.

If compromise is found, treat the entire SD-WAN fabric as the blast radius. Recommended actions include rotating credentials, reviewing administrator activity, validating device states, and restoring the orchestrator from trusted sources.
Separately, CVE-2025-68686 in Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN and CVE-2026-16723 in Alibaba's Fastjson library (CVSS 9.0, unpatched) are also under active attack, highlighting broader threats.
